text:
The current program has three faults. M1 sits in triode because its Vgs is pinned at 0.75 V by the input bias, yet it was sized by gm/Id as if it were free. The M0/M4 sink is sized independently, so the pb node is off (M3 carries 4.5 µA, not 5 µA). The M2:M3 ratio also comes out around 8.6 rather than 11. I'm switching to sizing M1 by current at its fixed Vgs, deriving the load current from the LUT, and making M4 an exact width-scaled copy of M0.

```json
{"action": "edit", "reason": "M1 is triode because it was sized by gm/Id while Vgs is fixed at 0.75 V by the input bias, so its width must be set by current at that Vgs. M4 and M0 are sized independently, which corrupts the pb bias. The new program sizes M1 from its current at fixed Vgs, sets I1 from the predicted load current, and makes M4 an exact width-scaled copy of M0."}
```

```python
PARAMS = {
    "L1":    (0.3, 0.15, 1.0),     # NMOS CS length (Vgs fixed at 0.75 V by input bias)
    "gmid2": (11.0, 9.5, 12.0),    # PMOS load/reference gm/Id (higher -> lower vdsat, eats less swing)
    "L2":    (0.3, 0.25, 0.3),     # PMOS load/reference length (same on M2 and M3)
    "IREF":  (5e-6, 4e-6, 6e-6),   # PMOS reference current (M3 diode)
    "K2":    (12.0, 10.0, 13.0),   # mirror ratio M2:M3 (integer)
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    VDD = 1.8
    cl = spec.get("cl", 5e-13)
    iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)   # testbench reference current into ibias
    IREF = p["IREF"]
    L1 = p["L1"]
    L2 = p["L2"]
    K = int(round(p["K2"]))

    VGS1 = 0.75     # fixed by input DC bias
    VDS1 = 0.9      # target output DC level (M1 must stay saturated here)

    # --- PMOS load mirror: M3 = 1x unit (diode), M2 = Kx unit, same L ---
    opr = lut.size("p", p["gmid2"], L2, IREF, vds=0.9)
    W_unit = opr.W
    op2 = lut.op("p", W_unit * K, L2, opr.vgs, VDS1)     # load at the operating point
    I2 = op2["Id"]                                        # actual load current at Vsd ~ 0.9 V

    # --- NMOS CS M1: current I1 = I2 (balances the output at VDS1), width from current at fixed Vgs ---
    I1 = I2
    t = lut.op("n", 10.0, L1, VGS1, VDS1)
    W1 = 10.0 * I1 / t["Id"]                              # Id is ~linear in W at fixed Vgs/Vds
    op1 = lut.op("n", W1, L1, VGS1, VDS1)

    # --- NMOS sink mirror: M0 diode at testbench iref, M4 = width-scaled copy sinking IREF ---
    op0 = lut.size("n", 10, 1.0, iref, vds=0.6)
    W4 = op0.W * IREF / iref
    L0 = 1.0

    n = Netlist("vin vout vdd vss ibias")
    n.M("M1", "vout", "vin", "vss", "vss", "nfet", W1, L1)           # signal NMOS CS
    n.M("M2", "vout", "pb", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", W_unit * K, L2)    # PMOS load, K x unit
    n.dev("M3", "pb", "pb", "vdd", "vdd", opr)                       # PMOS diode, 1x unit
    n.M("M4", "pb", "ibias", "vss", "vss", "nfet", W4, L0)           # NMOS sink: IREF
    n.dev("M0", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", op0)                 # NMOS diode at ibias

    # --- analytic predictions ---
    gm1 = op1["gm"]
    gds1 = op1["gds"]
    gds2 = op2["gds"]
    gain = gm1 / (gds1 + gds2)
    f3db = (gds1 + gds2) / (2 * PI * cl)
    gbw = gm1 / (2 * PI * cl)
    power = VDD * (I1 + iref + IREF)
    swing = (VDD - opr.vdsat) - op1["vdsat"]

    return n, {
        "gain_db": db(gain),
        "f3dB": f3db,
        "gbw": gbw,
        "power": power,
        "vout_dc": VDS1,
        "swing": swing,
    }
```
